name: UGA Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own title page names one champion: Chainsaw Charlie, crowned in the promotion's own "Ultimate Quest" tournament at Summer Breakout 2001 — the only reign the held record attests under the UGA name itself, distinct from the fed's own earlier WWC-era Heavyweight lineage (see the WWC World Heavyweight Championship's own separate record).
notes: This reign's own source (title.html, geocities.com, YAHOOIDS/C/o/Colosseum/Park/8978) is an UNSERVED raw file in this accession's own vault mirror, not one of this wing's four served documents — a prior tier-1 pass's own citation named a served page that does not exist, corrected 2026-08-31 after verifying the claim directly against the raw file (see the reign's own won.source). The same raw page also carries this wing's own UGA Television and Super J-Crown Cup title lineages and two then-vacant titles (International, King of Hardcore), none of which are registered — a pending-enrichment lead for a future formal serving pass.

name: WWC World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a full eighteen-champion chain across the promotion's WWC era (1997-2001), before the WWC name itself gave way to UGA — seventeen of the eighteen reigns are structured here, the page's own numbering skipping from a 14th to a 16th champion, an archival gap in the source itself, never filled. "The Franchise" Shane Stud held the title five times, more than any other champion the ledger names; the chain closes on his own fifth and final recorded reign, won at Carnacage III (31 December 1999, billed the last-ever Carnacage) over Disturbed Youth, the man who had beaten him for the belt eleven days earlier in the WWC's own first-ever Canadian title change.

name: WWC Hardcore Championship
epitaph: Contested in a Triple Hardcore Challenge culminating in a bloody four-way dance at Carnacage 99, where Street Punk pinned Joe Snow to become the fed's own only attested WWC Hardcore Champion. No prior champion or title history is named in the held record.

name: WWC World Television Championship
epitaph: Mad Dog Mortimer's own defense against Mighty Ryan Kelly at Carnacage 99 ended in controversy: a suspended referee, Frat Boy, came out uninvited and counted the pinfall for Kelly, "apparently" — the fed's own recap's own hedge — making him champion. No prior reign data survives for Mortimer's own title win.

name: WWC International Championship
epitaph: Larry Gionet held the WWC International Championship into Carnacage 99, retaining it by disqualification against The Jester after Jago Ripley and The Beast ran in. No document held records when or how Gionet won the title.
